# Jeremiah 19 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The LORD said, "Go and buy a clay jar from a potter. Then take some of the leading citizens and senior priests

**2** The LORD pronounced judgment on Jerusalem for the terrible things done in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom.

**3** and say to them, 'Listen to the word of the LORD, you kings of Judah and people of Jerusalem! The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to bring such a terrible disaster on this place that the ears of everyone who hears about it will ring!

**4** The LORD pronounced judgment on Jerusalem for the terrible things done in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom.

**5** They have built pagan shrines to Baal and there they burn their own children as sacrifices to Baal. I never commanded such a horrible thing — it never even crossed My mind!

**6** The LORD pronounced judgment on Jerusalem for the terrible things done in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom.

**7** The LORD pronounced judgment on Jerusalem for the terrible things done in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom.

**8** The LORD pronounced judgment on Jerusalem for the terrible things done in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom.

**9** The LORD pronounced judgment on Jerusalem for the terrible things done in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom.

**10** "Then break the jar in front of the men who came with you

**11** and tell them, 'This is what the LORD of Armies says: I will shatter this nation and this city, just as this clay jar has been shattered beyond repair.'"

**12** The LORD pronounced judgment on Jerusalem for the terrible things done in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom.

**13** The LORD pronounced judgment on Jerusalem for the terrible things done in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom.

**14** The LORD pronounced judgment on Jerusalem for the terrible things done in the Valley of Ben-Hinnom.

**15** "This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I'm going to bring down on this city and its surrounding towns every disaster I have announced against them, because they stubbornly refuse to listen to Me."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **19:1**: Jeremiah addresses the shattered flask — a message that confronted the comfortable assumptions of his audience.

- **19:7**: The broken vessel image captures something profound — a truth the original audience would have immediately felt in their bones.

- **19:15**: God seals this message with His signature declaration — 'I have spoken' — leaving no room for negotiation.

— PNEUMA
